## Physical Activity

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Physical activity meeting guidelines
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
activity_guidelines <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Activity_Guidelines.csv")

# Data wrangling
activity_guidelines <- activity_guidelines %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(met_2014_guidelines_for_age_group_18_64_years_n:did_not_meet_2014_guidelines_for_age_group_18_64_years_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(guidelines_n    = met_2014_guidelines_for_age_group_18_64_years_n,
                notguidelines_n = did_not_meet_2014_guidelines_for_age_group_18_64_years_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(guidelines_n:notguidelines_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("guidelines"),
                starts_with("notguidelines"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "guidelines"    = "Met guideline",
                                              "notguidelines" = "Did not meet guideline",
                                              "answered"      = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Met guideline",
                                           "Did not meet guideline",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Type of physical activity
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
activity_type <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Activity_Type.csv")

# Data wrangling
activity_type <- activity_type %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(moderate_n = moderate_physical_activity_excl_workplace_n + moderate_workplace_physical_activity_n,
                vigorous_n = vigorous_physical_activity_excl_workplace_n + vigorous_workplace_physical_activity_n,
                answered_n = total_n - not_applicable_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(walkingexercise_n = walking_for_exercise_recreation_or_sport_n,
                walkingtravel_n   = walking_to_get_to_places_n,
                strength_n        = strength_or_toning_n,
                none_n            = no_physical_activity_in_last_week_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(-moderate_physical_activity_excl_workplace_n,
                -moderate_workplace_physical_activity_n,
                -vigorous_physical_activity_excl_workplace_n,
                -vigorous_workplace_physical_activity_n,
                -not_applicable_n,
                -total_n) %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(walkingexercise_n:vigorous_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("none"),
                starts_with("walkingtravel"),
                starts_with("walkingexercise"),
                starts_with("strength"),
                starts_with("moderate"),
                starts_with("vigorous"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "none"            = "No activity",
                                              "walkingtravel"   = "Walking for travel",
                                              "walkingexercise" = "Walking for exercise",
                                              "strength"        = "Strength or toning",
                                              "moderate"        = "Moderate intensity",
                                              "vigorous"        = "Vigorous intensity",
                                              "answered"        = "Total"),
                                levels = c("No activity",
                                           "Walking for travel",
                                           "Walking for exercise",
                                           "Strength or toning",
                                           "Moderate intensity",
                                           "Vigorous intensity",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 11% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 15 years and over) living in Greater Melbourne met the weekly physical activity guidelines, which [recommend a minimum level of weekly physical activity](https://www.health.gov.au/topics/physical-activity-and-exercise/physical-activity-and-exercise-guidelines-for-all-australians) based on age and the types of activity undertaken. This equates to approximately 2,300 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults.

- Males were more likely to have met the weekly physical activity guidelines than females (15% vs. 4.5%).

- The most commonly reported type of physical activity undertaken by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne during the week prior to the survey was walking to get to places (44%) followed by moderate physical activity (41%).

- 19% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents aged 15 years and over living in Greater Melbourne reported no physical activity during the week prior to the survey. Females were more likely to report no physical activity than males (27% vs. 12%).

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report, it was noted that only a small percentage of people were not engaging in any activity at all. This was thought to be due to a strong culture of community participation in sport, such as regular sporting carnivals.

- Of particular note within the NEPHU catchment was the [Fitzroy Stars Football and Netball Club](https://aal.org.au/the-fitzroy-stars-football-netball-club-fsfnc/), a community based organization that utilises sport to engage the local Aboriginal community. Participation in this club, and in sport more broadly, was discussed as providing not only health benefits but also social and cultural benefits.

- Competing priorities such as carer responsibilities were discussed as a contributing factor for people who were not engaging in physical activity.

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people aged 15 years and over completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- What types of physical activity did you do last week?
  - Walking continuously for ten minutes or more
  - Moderate activity
  - Vigorous activity
  - None of the above
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- What types of walking, moderate, or vigorous activity did you do continuously for ten minutes or more last week? (select all that apply)
  - Walking for exercise, recreation, or sport
  - Walking to get to places
  - Moderate activity for exercise
  - Moderate activity while working
  - Vigorous activity for exercise
  - Vigorous activity while working
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Did you do any strength and toning activities last week?
  - Yes
  - No

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

- Physical activity was assessed using the [2014 Australian Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines](https://www.health.gov.au/topics/physical-activity-and-exercise/physical-activity-and-exercise-guidelines-for-all-australians).
  - The Guidelines recommend a minimum level of physical activity during the week based on age and the types of activity undertaken.
  - The moderate and vigorous intensity categories include physical activity undertaken both at work and outside of work.

## Mode of Transport to Work

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mode of transport to work, by LGA
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
transport_lga <- f_read_census_lga("Aboriginal_Activity_Transport_LGA.csv",
                                   variable = "transport") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!transport %in% c("Mode not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
transport_lga <- transport_lga %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(transport = dplyr::case_when(
    transport == "Worked at home or Did not go to work" ~ "WFH or did not work",
    TRUE ~ transport)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_lga(variable = transport,
                       level    = "person",
                       dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(active_prop   = aboriginal_n_active_transport / aboriginal_total * 100,
                public_prop   = aboriginal_n_public_transport / aboriginal_total * 100,
                vehicle_prop  = aboriginal_n_vehicle / aboriginal_total * 100,
                other_prop    = aboriginal_n_other_mode / aboriginal_total * 100,
                notravel_prop = aboriginal_n_wfh_or_did_not_work / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(lga_name,
                active_n = aboriginal_n_active_transport,
                active_prop,
                public_n = aboriginal_n_public_transport,
                public_prop,
                other_n = aboriginal_n_other_mode,
                other_prop,
                vehicle_n = aboriginal_n_vehicle,
                vehicle_prop,
                notravel_n = aboriginal_n_wfh_or_did_not_work,
                notravel_prop,
                aboriginal_total)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mode of transport to work, by age and sex
# Data from ABS Census using TableBuilderPro
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in Census data
transport_agesex <- f_read_census_agesex("Aboriginal_Activity_Transport_AgeSex.csv",
                                         variable = "transport") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::filter(!transport %in% c("Mode not stated", "Not applicable"))

# Data wrangling
transport_agesex <- transport_agesex %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(transport = dplyr::case_when(
    transport == "Worked at home or Did not go to work" ~ "WFH or did not work",
    TRUE ~ transport)) %>% 
  #
  f_wrangle_census_agesex(variable = transport,
                          dichot   = "no") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(aboriginal_total = aboriginal_n_active_transport + aboriginal_n_public_transport + aboriginal_n_vehicle + aboriginal_n_other_mode + aboriginal_n_wfh_or_did_not_work,
                #
                active_prop   = aboriginal_n_active_transport / aboriginal_total * 100,
                public_prop   = aboriginal_n_public_transport / aboriginal_total * 100,
                vehicle_prop  = aboriginal_n_vehicle / aboriginal_total * 100,
                other_prop    = aboriginal_n_other_mode / aboriginal_total * 100,
                notravel_prop = aboriginal_n_wfh_or_did_not_work / aboriginal_total * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.na(.), 0)),
                across(where(is.numeric), ~replace(., is.nan(.), 0))) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(age_group,
                sex,
                active_n = aboriginal_n_active_transport,
                active_prop,
                public_n = aboriginal_n_public_transport,
                public_prop,
                other_n = aboriginal_n_other_mode,
                other_prop,
                vehicle_n = aboriginal_n_vehicle,
                vehicle_prop,
                notravel_n = aboriginal_n_wfh_or_did_not_work,
                notravel_prop,
                aboriginal_total)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [ABS Census 2021](https://www.abs.gov.au/census).

- Overall, 2.5% (n = 124) of people living in the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census took an active mode of transport to work and a further 5.6% (n = 279) took public transport. This was similar to the percentage of non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment who took an active mode of transport to work (2.4%) and higher than the percentage of non-Indigenous people living in the NEPHU catchment who took public transport (4.9%).

- The number of people living in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who used an active mode of transport or took public transport to work ranged from 76 (Darebin LGA) to 3 (Manningham LGA).

- The percentage of people in different LGAs within the NEPHU catchment who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander in the Census who used an active mode of transport or took public transport to work ranged from 20% (Yarra LGA) to 2.2% (Manningham LGA).

- Younger people were more likely to use an active mode of transport or public transport.

`r note_caveat_multipleresponse`

- In cases where the combination of responses contained 'Did not go to work', 'Worked at home', or 'Walked only', then these unique responses override any others.

- A number of regions across the state were in various stages of lockdown on 2021 Census night and during the week preceding it, resulting in a greater number of people working from home during this time. Working from home was included in the ‘Did not travel’ category.
